public_problem.summary: GitHub is expanding agentic repository work while adding security validation, policy-constrained agentic workflows, approval boundaries, and platform-level lifecycle/authorization concerns for coding agents.

official_sources.title: Security validation for third-party coding agents
GitHub Agentic Workflows is now in public preview
Bot-created pull requests can run workflows if approved
Staff Software Engineer — Mission Control, job 5611

bottleneck: Agent-generated repository changes need a trustworthy promotion boundary that binds the intended change, current reference state, required validation, authorized approval, unambiguous check evidence, exact mutation bytes, provider result, eventual-state reconciliation, post-action readback, replay behavior, and durable evidence.
reusable_invariant: A repository mutation is complete only when the exact intended bytes were authorized against the expected reference head, required check evidence is unique and well formed, required gates passed, bounded authority executed the mutation once, provider state reconciled to the returned mutation identity, reference readback confirmed it, replay could not duplicate it, and a terminal receipt preserved the result.
transfer_argument: GlacierEQ independently implemented and reproduced a governed GitHub mutation path that binds exact change identity, expected repository state, required validation, bounded approval, short-lived repository authority, exact provider bytes, provider mutation identity, bounded eventual-state reconciliation, reference readback, replay suppression, and receipt evidence. The reference specialist has now completed a measured evolution cycle that rejects contradictory or malformed check evidence before provider access. This proof-bound company-specific claim remains transferable engineering evidence for the public GitHub operating problem; it is not GitHub adoption evidence.

current_proof.observed: The reference Apex provider proof remains preserved: 26/26 exact Merge Authority tests and 38/38 proof-host gateway tests passed, a real disposable-branch provider mutation reconciled to reference readback, replay returned DUPLICATE_ALREADY_COMPLETED, the short-lived token was revoked, and target main remained unchanged. The evolved control logic was then measured against reference head f791c85a81768e72446619b39b5312ef1c768a02: the baseline accepted contradictory duplicate security evidence by last-write-wins normalization, while exact candidate bytes rejected it. Public proof-host CI passed 21/21 tests and the winner was merged to Apex main at 346b330bbfd705579b3a4d10d298a89493a98ee6 with exact source/test blob readback.
current_proof.limitation: The evolution proof does not perform a new GitHub provider mutation; the prior real-provider proof remains the provider evidence. The Apex repository remains private, but the exact three-file evolution candidate used by public proof PR #269 is publicly visible on the proof host. No GitHub adoption, employment, endorsement, GitHub production deployment, production-scale reliability, latency, throughput, or durability is established.

next_company_gate: Maintain proof and projection freshness at the proof_bound_company_specific ceiling. Any claim of GitHub adoption, GitHub production deployment, or production-scale reliability requires new public evidence and an additional gate; none is claimed here.
